title: Varicose veins: from valve failure to the right treatment
summary: Find out why varicose veins form, how to examine and image them, and which treatment the exam and current practice each expect.
closing: Duplex first, deep veins checked, ablation before the knife, ABPI before the bandage: that is the leg you can now manage.

objectives.text: Name the commonest vein, reflux site and type of varicose veins, and apply the CEAP 3 mm definition
Predict flow direction through perforators and what the calf pump does to leg venous pressure in reflux
Place the great and short saphenous veins and the named perforators (Cockett, Boyd, Dodd, Hunter) correctly
Pick the nerve at risk for GSV versus SSV surgery and the lower limit of GSV stripping
Place a venous ulcer by site and tell skin changes and CEAP classes apart
Tell the Brodie-Trendelenburg test from the Perthes test and read each result
Decide whether superficial vein surgery can go ahead by checking deep vein patency first
Choose the investigation of choice and the role of Doppler and venography
Pick the first-line treatment of truncal reflux, the next step if unsuitable, and who gets stockings
Choose foam versus liquid sclerotherapy and the sclerosant (STS or polidocanol)
Pick the step before compression for a venous ulcer, its mainstay treatment and the malignancy to biopsy for
Tell a saphena varix from a femoral hernia at the bedside

traps.trap: Trendelenburg operation with stripping is the first-line treatment for SFJ incompetence
A bedside Doppler, clinical test or venography is the investigation of choice for varicose veins (merged TR3: venography stretched to superficial reflux)
The Perthes test detects SFJ incompetence and the Brodie-Trendelenburg test detects deep vein patency
On the Brodie-Trendelenburg test, filling with the tourniquet still on means SFJ incompetence
The Trendelenburg test, operation, position and sign are one thing
The great and short saphenous veins run and terminate the same way
The saphenous nerve is at risk in short saphenous surgery; the sural nerve in GSV stripping
The GSV is stripped all the way to the ankle
Named perforators are interchangeable or placed at the wrong level
Perforator valves let blood flow from deep to superficial veins
Walking raises venous pressure in the leg; the calf pump produces ambulatory venous hypertension
CEAP diameter bands and ulcer-class numbers are interchangeable (merged TR15: C4, C5, C6 order)
Compression is started for a venous ulcer without measuring ABPI first
Compression stockings are the treatment for symptomatic varicose veins
Superficial vein stripping or ligation can be done without checking the deep veins
The most common finding is the only one (SFJ is the only site of reflux; primary is the only type)
Foam sclerotherapy suits telangiectasias; liquid sclerotherapy suits large truncal veins
Polidocanol is wrong as the sclerosant because the classic answer is STS
A saphena varix and a femoral hernia share a fluid thrill and both disappear on lying down
A venous ulcer sits on the toes, heel or lateral malleolus (the arterial sites)

segments.title: Varicose veins: the commonest of everything
segments.goal: Open with a groin-to-calf varicose vein stem the learner cannot fully answer, surfacing the 'commonest is the only' and GSV/SSV look-alike errors.
segments.notes: TR19 probe 1 (recognition) offers no trap option in the trap map: authors must add one (e.g. 'SFJ is the only site of reflux' or 'varicose veins are always primary').

prefer.reason: hook winner in stats and playbook (productive failure then retry in a different form)

segments.title: Why valves fail: flow, pump and pressure
segments.goal: Build the mental model of one-way perforator flow, the calf pump and ambulatory venous hypertension, then place the saphenous veins and named perforators on it.
segments.notes: Use predict-then-show for TR11 and TR12 (reversed mechanism); TR10 gets a rebuild-the-set repair.

segments.title: The leg and groin: ulcer site, CEAP, varix
segments.goal: From vignettes, place the venous ulcer, read skin changes and CEAP class, and separate saphena varix from femoral hernia.
segments.notes: TR24 probe 2 (which-is-not) offers no trap option: it lives in S7 and authors must add one there (e.g. a false varix-vs-hernia feature). Here use the vignette probe.

prefer.reason: clinical winner in stats; vignette pairs with second explanation

segments.title: Bedside tests, duplex and the deep-vein check
segments.goal: Separate Brodie-Trendelenburg from Perthes, choose duplex as the investigation of choice, and see why deep veins are checked before surgery.
segments.notes: Keep TR4 and TR5 sharing the Perthes and Brodie-Trendelenburg cases. TR2 recognition and vignette here; third probe in S7. TR18 first probe is the sequence form; later forms in S6 and S8.

prefer.reason: faded worked example with skip lane wins diagnosis; put the mechanism probe before the fork

segments.title: The treatment ladder and sclerotherapy
segments.goal: Pick the current first-line truncal reflux treatment against the PYQ key, who gets stockings, and the foam versus liquid and sclerosant choice.
segments.notes: TR22 probe 1 (recognition) offers no trap option: authors must add one (e.g. 'polidocanol is wrong because STS is the classic answer'). TR1 and TR17 share the management vignette; TR21 and TR22 share one sclerotherapy stem. Teach both the PYQ key and current practice (K119, K126).

prefer.reason: erroneous example suits the old-PYQ-key versus current-practice conflict

segments.title: Operating safely, and the ulcer leg
segments.goal: Decide the extent of stripping, the nerve at risk, the deep-vein precondition, and the ABPI-first rule with compression for an ulcer.
segments.notes: TR9 then TR8 share the anatomy-to-complication thread. TR18 vignette here; TR17 contrast re-test on ulcer compression. TR16 sequence then vignette.

prefer.reason: management winner in stats; worked ulcer case with last step faded

segments.title: Exam traps: which is NOT
segments.goal: Run the which-is-not and look-alike stems where several traps are tested at once.
segments.notes: TR2 probe 3, TR4 probe 3, TR19 probe 2 and TR24 probe 2 are which-is-not. TR2 probe 3 and TR4 probe 3 and TR24 probe 2 offer no trap option in the trap map: authors must add at least one trap option to each (e.g. TR2: 'venography is the gold standard'; TR4: 'Perthes detects SFJ incompetence'; TR24: 'a saphena varix has a bruit/does not reduce on lying down'). Each probe must tag every distractor to one trap.

prefer.reason: exam-trap drill fits which-is-not stems; T7 contrast as alternate

segments.title: Mixed quiz: new stems
segments.goal: Short cold quiz of 8 to 10 new mixed stems that re-test the highest-yield traps in fresh forms.
segments.notes: Playbook: 8 to 10 NEW stems, not a replay of earlier items; at least one probe with no hint option; no new teaching.

prefer.reason: playbook: consolidate cold-check with most distinct trap-mapped distractors; hint-then-retry on misses
